deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is a continuous German prose passage of historical lecture or reading notes on ancient Greek history, specifically the Third Sacred War (356–346 BC). It continues directly from folio 111, which gives the war's cause: the Phocians seized land sacred to Delphi, were fined by the Amphictyonic Council, refused to pay, and Thebes was charged with enforcement in 356. Folio 113 continues with Philip's later campaigns (Elatea in 339, Chaeronea in 338).

Content of this page:
(1) The Phocians, previously too weak to resist, plundered the rich Delphic oracle in their territory and used the treasure to hire mercenaries.
(2) Their leader was Philomelus, who died in 353 while invading Boeotia.
(3) His brother Onomarchus succeeded him and carried the war into Thessaly. There Philip of Macedon defeated him, and Onomarchus was killed (352).
(4) The 'third brother' Phayllus followed. The war dragged on and was ended only by Philip.
(5) Philip fell upon the Phocians, who lost most of their land and their seat and vote in the Amphictyonic Council. Philip had himself enrolled in the Council (the sentence continues on the next page with 'auch').

There is no derivation to reconstruct. The handwriting is a fairly regular, rounded Kurrent and does not obviously look like Gauss's own hand. This may be a copied set of lecture notes (perhaps on universal or Greek history) bound into the bundle. That is a suspicion only; I cannot confirm whose hand it is.
errors: Historical, not mathematical: Philomelus is usually dated to have died in 354 BC (battle of Neon, near Tithorea, against Boeotians and Locrians), not 353. Some chronologies give 354/353, so this is a minor point.

Historical: the brothership of Philomelus, Onomarchus and Phayllus follows a tradition found in Diodorus. Some ancient sources and modern scholars treat Onomarchus as a colleague rather than a brother of Philomelus.
Historical omission: after Phayllus (died c. 351) the Phocian command passed to Phalaecus, who surrendered to Philip in 346. The notes skip him.
The war's end ('erst durch Philipp geendigt') is undated here; it was 346 BC (Peace of Philocrates and the Phocian capitulation).

results.what: Narrative notes on the Third Sacred War (Phocian plundering of Delphi, Philomelus, Onomarchus, Phayllus, Philip II's intervention, Phocian expulsion from the Amphictyony)
results.modern_name: Third Sacred War (356–346 BC), ancient Greek history
results.usually_credited_to: Standard textbook history based on Diodorus Siculus XVI

deep.surprise_reason: The page is purely historical narrative with no mathematical content. It may not even be in Gauss's hand. Nothing here bears on the history of mathematics.

checkable.asserts: The Sacred War as dated in the notes (begun 356, ended 346 by Philip) lasted 10 years, consistent with '10 Jahr dauerten' on folio 111.
Onomarchus' death (352) falls one year after the date given for Philomelus' death (353), per the notes' internal chronology.
